title: Equal pH does not mean equal buffer capacity
promptMarkdown: Two ideal hypothetical buffers have $\mathrm pK_a=4.70$ and final volume $0.500\,\mathrm L$. Buffer P contains $0.0300$ mol HA and $0.0200$ mol A$^-$. Buffer Q contains one tenth of each amount. Estimate their initial pH. Now consider a separate addition of $0.00500$ mol strong acid to each, with negligible volume change. Determine which remains a buffer, estimate each final pH with suitable assumptions, and explain what an actual activity-based calculation would require.
hintLadder: Neutralisation happens before the remaining weak equilibrium is solved.
Count the available conjugate-base moles in each buffer.
After a component is exhausted, retain the excess strong acid in the charge balance.

criteria.criterion: Uses the correct post-neutralisation inventories in both solutions.
